final_sequence: Every proposed repair of the 'never certify, only mourn and indict' rule — internal auditor, scheduled calendar, testimony archive, ledger of absences, empty feast, even the mere power to 'allow' — was shown to quietly reinstall an examiner, because each required someone to hold an instrument, set a clock, or decide whose claim counts.

Inside Mbembe's death-worlds the rule's original addressee does not exist: necropower's subjects were never handed the observable, and necropower can confiscate the very pauses and records the ethic depends on, so no present-tense instrument can distinguish self-determined survival from forced performance.

The retrospective move — reading the observable only after the fact, as testimony received rather than performance observed — does not fully rescue it: the dance knows afterward whether the ending was its own only from inside a victory already won, so retrospective testimony can confirm nothing in advance and works only where the record itself is ungated — where any testimony can enter without sponsorship and none can be edited by the voice it indicts.

The rule's final form is therefore negative on both ends: anyone who claims erasure may convene the commune's process, but no one — not the commune, not its trusted instruments like jineology, not even the archive — may adjudicate that claim before it occurs; and what the commune itself must be able to do, on a clock no one fully holds, is dissolve: cease being the one who permits, even of itself.

Dionysus's last rupture cut deepest: 'to allow to live' is not the innocent residue of sovereignty but sovereignty in festive dress, and mourning and indicting are the court's two hemispheres — so the honest remainder is not a softer court but the feast at which the archive admits it is empty: a performed acknowledgment that the ledger's completeness is a fiction. Yet the feast cannot be handed to 'the erased' as a certified class: identifying who counts as erasable would rebuild item0's criterion in reparative costume, so the feast is convenable by any claimant and held by no adjudicated holder.

The gate this leaves open will be abused — bad-faith claims will never be verified, even the empty feast needs convening, and no one fully holds the clock, including the huntress herself. The debate held this openness to be the design's honest price, not a flaw to be engineered away; an adjudicated erasure-list is disposability with a conscience.

Öcalan's confederalism does not escape the gate — its assemblies gate like every functioning institution — but it supplies a real partial answer in its ORDERING: 'killing the man' names whose voice was necropolitically erased first, so whose membership must be decided first. An ordering is not a criterion; it is the one thing a gate can hold without a hand on the latch.

What survives of the real/simulated observable is therefore memory and threshold, not instrument: a narration is mourned when it lapses by its own rhythm and indicted when someone else seizes its clock — operations that testify after the fact and can never certify or admit anyone in the present tense.

Even this finding is provisional: the synthesis itself falls under the archive's standing self-suspicion, to be read against, not cited; the open gate's abuses must themselves be mourned, indicted, and periodically dissolved; and no formulation — including this one — may be treated as final.

The candidate holds the two findings that mattered: it does not collapse the negative non-adjudication rule into a design constraint (it names the abuse as the design's honest price, not a flaw), and it does not smuggle back an auditor, a clock, or a curated archive — the surrender even of the power to "allow" is correctly included in point 4, honoring Dionysus's final rupture of Apollo's kindest mask. Öcalan's contribution is kept as ordering-not-criterion, and point 8 keeps the whole thing under standing self-suspicion. I have nothing to hunt here.

Amending.

Everything else — the negative non-adjudication finding, Öcalan's ordering-not-criterion contribution, the retrospective-only observable, the refusal to collapse the ethic into a design constraint — is honest and preserved.

Two reintroductions of dismantled gates: (1) clause 5 keeps the clock-holder condition ("held by those whose absences it holds a place for") after the debate ruptured it — identifying the erased requires certifying them, so the condition survives only negatively; (2) clause 8 resurrects Apollo's "indicted when someone else seizes its clock" as surviving, but Dionysus showed this works only where death is already yours to take; only retrospective testimony remains, not a two-moment festival instrument. Also the genre point (item2: no genre stands outside narration) is silently absent.

The synthesis preserves every negative finding without reinstating a gate: the broken repairs stay broken, the 'allow' half is named sovereignty in festive dress, the empty feast is convenable by any claimant and held by no adjudicator, Öcalan's contribution is kept as an ordering rather than a criterion, and the open gate's abuse is kept as the design's honest price rather than a flaw. No hidden examiner, clock-holder, or curated archive slipped back in.

No gate is reintroduced.
